prompt.context: Your client is the CEO of a leading diversified healthcare products and pharmaceuticals company called HealthCareCo. The company's principal business is the discovery, development, manufacture and sale of a broad and diversified line of healthcare products. HealthCareCo has about 50,000 employees in approximately 100 countries around the world. Currently, HealthCareCo has 4 different revenue-generating business units: pharmaceuticals, medical devices, health foods, and specialized surgery products. There are 3-4 main competitors; the client is ranked #2 or #3 in the market. Thinking ahead for the next 5 years, the CEO wants to distinguish the firm through innovation in the healthcare and pharma industry and has engaged McKinsey to help him consider cost optimization as one of the important elements of his strategy.
prompt.question: The CEO wants to consider cost optimization as a key element of his 5-year strategy. How would you approach this engagement?

clarifying_info.q: What is the CEO's primary goal — revenue growth, cost reduction, or both?
clarifying_info.a: The CEO is primarily focused on cost optimization to free up capital and improve competitiveness, while also aiming to differentiate through innovation.

clarifying_info.q: Has the company grown organically or through acquisitions?
clarifying_info.a: The company has grown through multiple acquisitions across its business units and geographies.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any specific cost areas or business units already identified as problems?
clarifying_info.a: No specific areas have been identified yet; the engagement is at the diagnostic stage.

clarifying_info.q: What is the time horizon for realizing cost savings?
clarifying_info.a: The CEO is thinking about the next 4-5 years.

exhibits.title: Income Statement - HealthCareCo
exhibits.shows: Income statement comparing HealthCareCo financials to industry benchmarks, showing net sales, COGS, R&D, Business Support costs, EPS, and other line items.

exhibits.title: Basic Support Function Costs Comparison
exhibits.shows: Bar charts comparing HealthCareCo vs benchmark costs (as % of some base) for four BSF functions: Finance, HR, Procurement, and Legal.

data.note: All four BSF functions (Finance, HR, Procurement, Legal) show HealthCareCo costs materially higher than benchmark; benchmark costs are approximately 30-40% lower than client costs across all functions shown.

exhibits.title: Activity Split across BSFs
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart showing the split between Transactional and Specialized activities within each of the four BSF functions (Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement) for a typical geographical sub-unit of a Business Unit.

exhibits.title: Outsourcing and Consolidation Framework
exhibits.shows: A geographic map or framework diagram showing two types of centers: Outsourced Centers (for Transactional Activities) and Centers of Excellence (for Specialized Activities), with legend indicating which locations handle which type.

exhibits.title: Basic Support Functions Cost % and Cost Savings Rates
exhibits.shows: Pie chart showing BSF cost breakdown by function (% of total $12B BSF), plus a bar chart showing cost savings rates (%) for each cost reduction lever: Center of Excellence, Outsourced Center, and IT Rationalization.

data.note: Facilities are local — ignore cost savings from Facilities

framework: Review financial reports: analyze income statement/balance sheet, key ratios, historical performance, and compare with competitors

Map the value chain and org structure across all 4 business units: primary functions (Inbound Ops, Company Ops, Outbound Ops, Marketing, Sales, Service) and support functions (Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Procurement, Facilities)
Benchmark against competitors: understand HCC's value proposition, target customers, and competitive positioning
Understand strategic direction: cost-based vs. value-based differentiation; note that pharma/healthcare requires R&D investment to compete on innovation
Assess market trends and industry factors: regulatory changes, foreign relations, taxes, FX implications given global operations

questions.prompt: Question 0: What key factors would you consider in preparation for your first meeting with the CEO and his team?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers: (1) Financial reports — income statement/balance sheet, key ratios, historical performance, competitor benchmarks; (2) Value chain / org structure — primary and support functions across all 4 BUs; (3) Competitor landscape — differentiation and value proposition; (4) Strategy — cost vs. innovation differentiation, role of R&D; (5) Market trends — global healthcare trends; (6) Regulatory/industry factors — patents, foreign exchange, tax, regulatory changes given 100-country footprint.

questions.prompt: Question 1: Review Exhibit 1 and share your initial thoughts and hypotheses.
questions.guidance: Strong candidates identify four key observations: (1) COGS is at par with industry (39% vs 40%) — not a major concern but worth monitoring; (2) R&D is below industry (10% vs 12%) — suggests HCC may be a 'follower' or competes in less R&D-intensive segments; tension with CEO's innovation ambition; (3) Business Support costs are significantly above industry (30% vs 25%) — the clearest cost reduction opportunity; (4) EPS is below industry ($2.00 vs $2.50) — a concern for shareholders. Synthesis: focus on Business Support Functions cost reduction; this would free capital for R&D investment to support the innovation strategy.

math.answer: HCC spends $2B more on Business Support than industry benchmark.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Business Support Functions (BSF) costs are high. Why do you think this might be the case?
questions.guidance: First, candidate should define BSF: non-revenue-generating functions necessary for operations (Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Procurement, Facilities). After reviewing Exhibit 2, candidate should note all four BSF functions are above benchmark by 30-40%. Strong answers for root causes: (1) Growth through acquisitions — each acquiree brought its own BSF headcount and complexity; (2) Geographic complexity — 100 countries means different local requirements; (3) Organizational complexity — 4 separate BUs each maintaining own BSF; (4) Siloed business units — no overlap or sharing of BSF tasks across BUs. Interviewer should push for 4-5 distinct reasons.

questions.prompt: Question 3: Your team analyzes activity types within each BSF function (see Exhibit 3). Can you think of ways to reduce BSF costs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first explain the distinction: Transactional = day-to-day, low-skill, repetitive; Specialized = high-skill, geography/BU-specific, requires multiple stakeholders. Observations: Finance and HR are predominantly transactional (70-80%); Legal and Procurement are predominantly specialized (60-70%), because they are inherently localized (contracts, regulations, language). Cost reduction ideas: (1) Eliminate redundant activities; (2) Automate transactional activities; (3) Improve process efficiency — reduce steps; (4) Reduce frequency of unnecessary activities; (5) Outsource certain activities. Bonus: candidate should proactively distinguish that outsourcing makes more sense for transactional vs. specialized work — transactional is more standardizable and location-independent.

questions.prompt: Question 4: Exhibit 4 shows a proposed outsourcing/consolidation approach. What do you think about it?
questions.guidance: Strong answer affirms the logic and explains why: Transactional activities → Outsourced Centers (global consolidation, e.g., India/Chile) because: cheap and available labor, expertise in services outsourcing, cost efficiency. Specialized activities → Centers of Excellence (regional consolidation) because: region-specific requirements, similar business environments, local laws/contracts/regulations, language considerations. This two-tier model matches the activity split identified in Exhibit 3.

questions.prompt: Question 5: The company ships transactional work to Outsourced Centers, specialized work to Centers of Excellence, and also does IT rationalization. Using Exhibit 5, how much cost savings will these changes generate?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate savings for each BSF function using: Finance/HR/Legal/Procurement savings = (Total BU Cost * Transactional% * 40% outsourced savings) + (Total BU Cost * Specialized% * 10% CoE savings). IT savings = IT Cost * 30%. Facilities excluded. An excellent candidate then connects back to Exhibit 1: industry BSF gap was $2B, but total savings of ~$2.33B exceed the gap — meaning additional savings can fund R&D, boost EPS, or be returned as dividends.

math.setup: Total BSF = $12B. Per function dollar amounts and activity splits from Exhibit 5. Savings rates: Outsourced Center = 40%, Center of Excellence = 10%, IT Rationalization = 30%.
math.answer: Total cost savings = approximately $2.33 billion. This exceeds the $2B BSF gap vs. industry benchmark, freeing additional capital for R&D and EPS improvement.

brainstorming.prompt: Why do you think HealthCareCo's Business Support Function costs are significantly higher than industry benchmarks across all functions?

categories.name: M&A / Growth History
ideas: Company grew through acquisitions — each acquired company added its own BSF headcount
Redundant systems and processes inherited from multiple acquisitions
Lack of post-merger integration of support functions

categories.name: Geographic Complexity
ideas: Operations in ~100 countries require locally adapted support functions
Different regulatory environments demand local legal and compliance teams
Foreign exchange and tax complexity adds overhead

categories.name: Organizational Structure
ideas: 4 separate business units each maintaining independent BSF teams
Siloed BUs with no sharing or overlap of support activities
No center-led model to capture economies of scale

categories.name: Process Inefficiency
ideas: Legacy processes that have not been modernized or automated
High manual / low-automation in transactional tasks
Duplication of effort across geographies for similar activities

categories.name: Technology
ideas: Fragmented IT systems across BUs and geographies
No common platforms or shared databases
Multiple ERP/HR/Finance systems running in parallel

recommendation: The CEO should engage in a large-scale organizational transformation to optimize Business Support Function costs. BSF costs are 5 percentage points above industry benchmark ($2B excess), are hurting competitive positioning, and are critical to fund the innovation strategy the CEO wants to pursue.

Specifically, create Outsourced Centers for transactional BSF activities (Finance, HR bookkeeping/payroll) and Centers of Excellence for specialized activities (Legal, Procurement), plus IT rationalization. This can deliver run-rate savings of approximately $2.33 billion.
risks: Downsizing repercussions — workforce reduction will require careful change management and may face legal/labor constraints in some geographies
Foreign limitations and extended implementation timeline — regulatory and cultural differences across 100 countries will complicate rollout
Operational disruption risk during transition — moving critical support functions carries execution risk
next_steps: Conduct full cost-benefit analysis: estimate total transformation cost and timeline to break-even on the $2.33B savings
Assess opportunity costs and alternative uses of saved capital (R&D investment, dividends, share buybacks)
Develop a change management plan to manage workforce implications and communicate the transformation to employees and investors
